Music, Art, Design and Technology
Subject Leads Claire Baldwin and Louise Young
At The Meads, our Music curriculum intends to inspire creativity and self-expression as well as giving the children opportunities to connect with others. Throughout their musical journey, we hope to foster a life-long love of music by exposing them to diverse musical experiences and igniting a passion for music. By listening and responding to different musical styles the children will find their voices as singers and performers and as composers, which will enable them to become confident, reflective musicians.
At The Meads, we aim for children to become confident and enthusiastic artists equipped with a range of techniques that they can creatively apply. They will be able to take inspiration from other artists and reflect on and evaluate their work to develop their own artwork and skills.
Design and Technology
At The Meads, our Design and Technology curriculum allows children to develop a broad range of knowledge, skills and understanding, and prompts engagement in a wide variety of activities. Children design and make products that solve real and relevant problems within a variety of contexts. Through evaluation of past and present Design and Technology, they develop a critical understanding of its impact on daily life and the wider world.

KS1 Reading and Phonics
As children begin to read in EYFS and KS1, we focus on decoding in daily phonics sessions using a structured Phonics programme called ‘Song of Sounds’. This then links to the reading scheme books with the children applying sounds that they have learnt in their phonics sessions to their reading. Children also learn to read using whole word recognition, rhyme and context. As children build fluency, further reading skills are developed including, re-telling, inference and prediction.
All children have the opportunity to visit our school library once a week. Children are encouraged to read a range of text types including fiction, non-fiction and poetry. They have the opportunity to talk about books and authors that they have enjoyed and extend their current reading experiences.

Diana Holmes: Co-opted Governor
Appointed by the Governing Body
Term of Office: 4 years to November 2028

I have been a parent at The Meads since we moved to East Grinstead in 2006. I was immediately struck by the caring community and warmth of staff, and my children have been very happy during their time here. I have been a member of the governing body since 2011 and became Chair of Governors in September 2020. The school has grown and changed considerably over the years, but wellbeing, inclusivity and the strive for ambitious outcomes for all pupils remain at its heart. It is a privilege to help strategically lead the school on its continuing journey to outstanding.
Away from The Meads, I work in an admin role at a local school for children with Autism and am also Clerk to their Governing Body.
Vice Chair of Governors

Michelle Adkin: Co-opted Governor

I have been a resident of East Grinstead since 1999, and live very close to The Meads with my two children, husband and small but confident dog!
My eldest started at The Meads in 2019, and I was immediately taken with how supportive and encouraging the staff are. I am excited to have been appointed co-opted governor, as this will be my way of contributing to the ongoing success of our school.
I have a number of years’ experience working within finance, in a variety of roles of both a statutory and an analytical capacity,
and I look forward to using my skillset to benefit the school.
Mr Matthew Hoyes: Parent Governor
Elected by Parents at the School
Term of Office: 4 years to November 2026
Health & Safety Governor
Co-Mental Health & Wellbeing Governor
I moved to East Grinstead in 2004 and both my boys attend The Meads. I have a background in aviation operations and I've been a volunteer youth worker in the town since 2005, as part of Jubilee Community Church, and from 2016-2022 worked full time as their children and youth leader. I enjoy being outdoors, adventuring in mud, and used to love playing rugby at EGRFC until my body let me know it was time to stop! I joined as a Parent Governor in November 2022 because, like all parents, I am passionate about contributing toward the vision of the school and helping where I can to improve the environment our children learn in.
Mrs Julie Fleming: Co-opted Governor
Appointed by the Governing Body
Term of Office: 4 years to January 2027
Equality & Community Cohesion Governor
I have been working in local secondary education for the past 15 years and I have also worked as a learning support assistant. I have run student and staff equalities groups and extra curricular public speaking, debate and enterprise clubs for students. As a parent, my own children attended East Grinstead schools and as a grandparent I am looking forward to going through it all again!
Local Authority Governor

appointed by the Governing Body

Head Teacher Performance Management Panel
Dr Christopher Manning: Parent Governor
Elected by Parents at the School
Term of Office: 4 years to November 2029
I was born and brought up in East Grinstead and now live in the town with my wife and two children, who both attend The Meads. In my professional life, I have worked in the environmental sector for over 25 years, starting out as a university lecturer before joining a government agency regulating the water industry. I am passionate about education and want all our children to feel safe, supported and inspired to learn. As such I am delighted to be a part of The Meads school community as a governor.
Mrs Stacey Leech: Parent Governor
Elected by Parents at the School
Term of Office: 4 years to November 2029
I live in East Grinstead with my husband and our son, who joined The Meads in 2024. In my professional life as a paediatric nurse, I place great importance on ensuring that every child’s voice is heard. I am passionate about making sure all children have the space, support, and opportunities they need to reach their full potential.
Outside of work, I love spending time outdoors and I’m a keen runner. I’m delighted to be part of the governing body and to contribute to the continued success and wellbeing of the school community.
Miss Melanie Essex: Co-opted Governor
Appointed by the Governing Body
Term of Office: 4 Years to November 2029
I have over 20 years’ experience working in finance, specialising in management accounting, alongside a background in education. Throughout my career, I have focused on supporting strong decision-making, developing people and systems, and bringing clarity to complex information. I particularly enjoy learning and teaching, and I value the role education plays in helping individuals reach their potential.
Outside of my professional role, I run a small, home-based cattery where the cat is always put first. Providing calm, individual care and ensuring each cat’s wellbeing is central to what I do, and it reflects my wider values of responsibility, compassion, and attention to detail.
I have a personal interest in the school, as my nephew attends, which gives me a strong connection to the school community and a genuine commitment to its success. As a governor, I am keen to use my skills and experience to support the school.
Mr Paul Tippett: Staff Governor
Elected by School Staff
Term of Office: 4 Years to Oct 2027
I am of British (Scottish and Cornish) parentage, but was born abroad, growing up in a variety of countries.
My later childhood was spent in Edinburgh, latterly studying for an M.A. in French and History of Art at Edinburgh University, with one year included studying in Paris. I then studied for a Post Graduate Diploma in Decorative Arts at the University of Glasgow, before lecturing in History of Art at that University. I then went on to work for auctioneers Christie’s for nearly twenty years, specialising in European Ceramics and Glass.
Once again drawn to teaching, I studied for a PGCE at Goldsmiths College in 2008. This included teaching placements in both London and south-west France. As an NQT, I then began my primary teaching career in London, working at a wide variety of schools in order to broaden my teaching experience.
I moved to Sussex in 2010, continuing to teach in primary education. I continue to explore my hobbies, which include travel, baking, gardening, keeping hens, antique dealing, walking my dogs and writing.
Miss Nicole Essex: Head Teacher
Statutory Member of the Governing Body
Mrs Fiona Mackay: Clerk To Governors
I recently joined The Meads as their Clerk to Governors and I am excited to take on this role. I have been in education for the last 11 years as an HLTA in a local primary school, but I was keen to take on a new challenge. Previously I have been, the chairperson for a local special needs pre-school called Opportunity Playgroup.
I was born in Yorkshire, but I moved to Scotland from the age of 5 returning to England in 1999 to take a new role as a Sales Consultant for a large Pensions and Life Assurance company in London. I moved to East Grinstead in November 2005 just in time for the birth of my first child. I love the county of Sussex, especially as a dog owner, the fantastic variety of countryside to explore.

At The Meads Primary School, developing understanding of the world is at that heart of our Science curriculum. Through building up a body of key knowledge and concepts, children are encouraged to develop a sense of excitement and curiosity about natural phenomena and the importance of science in every aspect of daily life.
The Science curriculum at our school endeavours to give children the curiosity, confidence and motivation to continue to further develop their skills into the next stage of their education and life experiences.
